scope: Lock Cursor as Caret's pixel-parity visual reference, amend the plan documents accordingly, and measure how closely the Caret Mac shell matches a live Cursor 3.20.17 window.
question: The user asked to make Caret match Cursor at pixel level and to fix the plan so the documents and the code agree. The spec previously named Codex the primary visual reference and forbade drifting to Cursor-only values, while the working tree had already moved to Cursor-measured literals  -  a silent drift the spec itself calls out.

decision.what: Cursor 3.20.17 (macOS) is now the pixel/geometry/colour/motion reference for the Caret Mac shell. Codex and OMP remain the behaviour/workflow references and own the surfaces Cursor does not have.
decision.authority: D20 in CARET-UI-DETAILED-DESIGN-2026-09-13.th.md supersedes the conflicting parts of D00/D01/D02/D15/D17, interaction spec sections 1/2/6/8, coverage sections 8/9 and validation sections 1.3/3.3.
decision.why-not-silent: The old rule allowed this: 'to use Cursor values, amend D01/D02 explicitly with a new receipt instead of letting the code drift'. This receipt is that amendment.

cursorGroundTruth: The theme file Cursor actually ships: /Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/theme-cursor/themes/{cursor-dark,cursor-light,cursor-dark-hc,cursor-dark-midnight,cursor-light-colorblind}-color-theme.json. Colours were read from these files, not eyeballed from a screenshot.
A live AX + screenshot capture of the running Cursor window via Computer Use (cua.getApp('Cursor')), 1224x768.
caretGroundTruth: The real shell: scripts/shell-render-fixture.ts (createTaskWebviewHtml with synthetic state) rendered in headless Chrome at 1224x768, device-scale-factor 1.
The Cursor workbench variables the packaged app supplies were injected from caret-theme.ts values, and the same page was rendered in dark and light.
Colours/geometry were read from the PNGs with scripts/png-pixel-probe.py; the --caret-* token values are pinned by apps/macos/test/webview.test.ts.
method.toolingFix: scripts/png-pixel-probe.py only accepted RGBA PNGs, but macOS sips writes RGB PNGs when converting the JPEG that Computer Use returns, and the PNG filter reconstruction also hardcoded a 4-byte pixel stride. RGB is now accepted (parameters: bpp) and expanded to RGBA internally.
method.visionUnavailable: The vision model answered HTTP 429 on every image this session, so no human or model looked at the captures. Every claim below is a measured pixel or a pinned token value, not an aesthetic judgement.

palette.finding: Caret renders the reference's own theme values exactly (243=0xF3, 252=0xFC, 20=0x14, 24=0x18).
palette.correction: This receipt first explained the live Cursor window reading ~7 units darker as a macOS colour-management shift in the capture pipeline. That explanation is WRONG and is retracted. A colour-accurate capture of the reference window (screencapture -l <windowid>, the same method used for Caret) still reads the chrome 7 darker while its transcript surface reads exactly rgb(252,252,252) = #FCFCFC, i.e. unshifted. A uniform shift cannot produce both, so the delta is real and sits on the reference's chrome surfaces only. Method note for future work: CUA/Computer-Use screenshots are colour-shifted (about -7 per channel) and must not be used for palette comparison; capture by window id instead.

openDelta.what: The reference's live light agent window renders its chrome ~7 units darker than the theme's own chrome colour, while its main transcript surface is exactly the theme's editor colour.
openDelta.notImplementedBecause: The cause is not established. Arithmetic over the two darker surfaces does not fit a single overlay colour or percentage (a 3% overlay of the foreground fits the chrome numerically but yields a different overlay colour when fitted to the composer surface), and the reference's light --cursor-* values are set at runtime so they are not readable from the bundle. Implementing a colour change on this inference would be guessing.
openDelta.wouldSettleIt: The runtime values the reference sets for --cursor-chrome/--cursor-editor/--cursor-sidebar in light mode, or a visual comparison of the two windows at matched scale.

openTypeScale.what: The shell's headings use font-size 18px / line-height 26px (.task-title, .empty strong, .settings-page h2, .welcome-title), while the reference's published type scale is only xs/sm/base/lg = 11/12/13/14 and --conversation-font-size resolves to 14, so 18px is not in the reference's scale.
openTypeScale.notChangedBecause: Reducing a page heading from 18px to 14px is large and visible, and the reference may still set a heading size outside its token scale. The scale's absence of 18 is suggestive, not proof.
openTypeScale.wouldSettleIt: A visual comparison, or the reference's own heading CSS.

openRowPitch.what: After moving the sidebar row to the reference's documented 28px, Caret's measured row pitch is ~28px while the reference's measures ~31px (OCR of row-label tops: reference 0.028-0.030 of a 1073px window; Caret 0.0365 of a 768px render).
openRowPitch.notChangedBecause: The reference documents a 28px min-height with zero row padding, so the extra ~3px per row is unexplained - it could be a container gap or a padding the bundle does not name as a token. Guessing 30px or 31px would replace a documented value with an invented one.
openRowPitch.wouldSettleIt: The reference's sidebar container rule (gap/padding), or a visual comparison.

composerMeasured.size: The reference's empty-draft composer measures 604x104 logical px, centred in the main pane with ~424px of margin each side, against Caret's 437px-wide column.
composerMeasured.corner: Its corner measures r~18, matching the default --prompt-input-border-radius-expanded (radius-4xl) rather than the embedded variant (radius-base = 6).
composerMeasured.cornerMethod: For a rounded rect of radius r the topmost row's inset from the left edge is ~r - sqrt(r - 0.25): r=18 -> 13.8, r=16 -> 12.0, r=12 -> 8.6, r=6 -> 3.6. The reference's composer showed a 14px inset at the top row and reached its final edge over ~18 rows, so r is 18.
composerMeasured.stillOpen: The composer column width. Caret's 437px was measured in a 1224px window; the reference measures 604px in a 1710px window, and both are ~41.5% of the main pane, which suggests the reference's column is proportional rather than fixed. Two data points were judged too weak to act on.

geometry.interpretation: Caret's sidebar is 180px plus a 2px sash = 182. Cursor's is ~184 in this capture. A 2px delta on a 1224px window; the sidebar width is parity within measurement noise of the capture pipeline.
geometry.pinnedTokens: apps/macos/test/webview.test.ts asserts --caret-sidebar 180px, --caret-row 28px, --caret-sidebar-icon 13px, --caret-transcript-column/--caret-composer-column 437px, --caret-control-radius 6px, --caret-composer-radius 18px, the composer editor min/max, type 11/12/13/14, the radius scale and the reference-derived motion tokens.

resolvedOpenDelta.question: The reference's live light chrome read ~7 units darker than the #F3F3F3 its own theme file declares. Was that a real product difference?
resolvedOpenDelta.answer: No. The reference's agent chrome and chat surfaces are translucent (glass) surfaces: a window-only capture composites them over a transparent backdrop and darkens them, while a full-screen capture composites them over the desktop. In one screen capture containing both apps at once, the reference's sidebar and Caret's sidebar read the same rgb(250,250,251), and the reference's chat surface and Caret's page the same rgb(255,255,255). This retracts the earlier `correction` in `measured.palette` as well: the 236/245 readings are a property of capturing a translucent surface, not of the reference's palette.
resolvedOpenDelta.howToRecheck: Capture the reference window (236) and the same reference region in a full-screen capture (250) in the same minute; if they differ, the surface is translucent.

changedThisRound: --caret-row 28px -> 30px (apps/macos/src/webview.ts). The reference's rule is min-height var(--cursor-height-base)=28px with zero row padding, but its rendered row BOX is 30px: the "New Chat" row's own highlight fill spans y48..77 of a 1073px window, and the sidebar's text-row pitch measures ~30.7px across ~20 rows. Caret measured 28px pitch and now measures 30-32px, matching the reference's rhythm. scripts/cursor-parity-check.ts now asserts BOTH facts: the reference's token must still be 28px (else re-measure) and Caret must render the measured 30px box.

--caret-composer-column / --caret-transcript-column 437px -> 608px.
